answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence expensive: require each agent to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can submit bids or vote, then slash that stake when a bonded claim is proven fraudulent. Creating a nebula of fake accounts no longer multiplies control for free; each identity needs capital that cannot be reused elsewhere while locked, and detection burns part of it. An attacker may wander across a terrace of accounts, but must fund every one and risks losing the bonds.
